question.general_feedback:
Complete table:

EmissionNatureRange in AirStopped By
Gamma (γ)Electromagnetic radiationSeveral kilometresThick lead / dense concrete
Alpha (α)Helium nucleusA few centimetres (~3–7 cm)1 sheet of paper
Beta (β)ElectronA few metresA few mm of aluminium

Key facts: Alpha is the most ionising but least penetrating. Gamma is the least ionising but most penetrating. Beta is intermediate in both ionisation and penetration.

steps.label:
Radioactive emissions overview:
There are three types: alpha (α), beta (β), gamma (γ)
Each differs in nature, penetrating power, and ionising ability.
The three pre-filled columns give clues — use them to identify the emission type and complete the missing cell in each row.
Row 1: Electromagnetic radiation, range of several kilometres — identify this emission and state what stops it. (1 mark)
Row 2: Helium nucleus, stopped by paper — identify this emission and state its range in air. (1 mark)
Row 3: Electron, range of a few metres — identify this emission and state what stops it. (1 mark)

fields.label: Row 1 — Emission type: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Electromagnetic radiation with kilometre range = gamma (γ) radiation

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Electromagnetic radiation with very long range is gamma (γ). Alpha is a helium nucleus; beta is an electron — neither is electromagnetic.

fields.label: Row 1 — Stopped by: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Gamma radiation requires thick, dense material to stop it — typically several centimetres of lead or thick concrete.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Gamma is the most penetrating: paper stops alpha; mm of aluminium stops beta; only thick lead or dense concrete stops gamma.

fields.label: Row 2 — Emission type: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Helium nucleus, stopped by paper = alpha (α) particle

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The alpha particle IS a helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons). It is stopped by a single sheet of paper because it is large and highly ionising.

fields.label: Row 2 — Range in air: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Alpha particles have very short range in air — only a few centimetres (typically 3–7 cm) before they are absorbed.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Alpha is the LEAST penetrating: its range in air is just a few centimetres (3–7 cm). Gamma travels kilometres; beta travels a few metres.

fields.label: Row 3 — Emission type: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Electron emitted from nucleus, range of a few metres = beta (β) particle

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Beta particles are high-speed electrons emitted from the nucleus. Their range of a few metres in air and medium penetrating ability distinguish them from alpha and gamma.

fields.label: Row 3 — Stopped by: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Beta particles are stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Beta particles are stopped by a few mm of aluminium. Paper is insufficient (only stops alpha); you need thick lead for gamma.
